name: Stationary bootstrap lower-bound Kelly
note: Four ordinary candidate rules run side by side, each carrying weight set by the WIDTH of its own Sharpe confidence interval rather than its centre. At every recompute each rule's trailing per-bar P&L is resampled B times by the Politis-Romano stationary bootstrap - geometric block lengths of mean blk, which is what keeps the resampled series stationary and stops an IID bootstrap handing back a far-too-tight interval on autocorrelated P&L - and the rule takes w = clip(SR_lcb/SR_point, 0, 1) * f_kelly where SR_lcb is the pct-th percentile of that distribution. A rule with SR_lcb <= 0 loses its vote and sits out until a later recompute clears it again; dead_n > 0 makes that retirement permanent after that many consecutive failures, and it defaults to 0 because on a run with a few dozen recomputes permanent retirement empties the panel on one bad early window and the family stops producing data at all; with dd_stop on, a rule whose live drawdown over the same window length exceeds the dd_pct-th percentile of its OWN resampled drawdowns is halted for stop_bars, on the argument that a drawdown deeper than its history can produce is evidence rather than luck. Sizing belongs to the shared harness, so the risk fraction becomes the weight the rule carries in the vote and the traded signal is the sign of the weighted sum - which makes f_kelly inert (a constant cannot change a sign), so it is declared but deliberately not swept. Block sums come from prefix sums and one set of draws is shared across rules, so a resample costs O(T*q) instead of O(T); the price of that is that resampled drawdown is measured at block resolution.
source: Politis, D. N. & Romano, J. P. (1994), 'The Stationary Bootstrap', Journal of the American Statistical Association 89(428), 1303-1313. Automatic block-length selection: Politis, D. N. & White, H. (2004), 'Automatic Block-Length Selection for the Dependent Bootstrap', Econometric Reviews 23(1), 53-70 (with the correction in Patton, Politis & White 2009). The under-betting rationale is standard Kelly estimation-risk analysis; combining it with a stationary-bootstrap lower bound and a bootstrap-drawdown stop is my synthesis.

import math
from collections import deque


def _ema(v, n):
    a = 2.0 / (n + 1.0)
    out = [None] * len(v)
    e = None
    for i, x in enumerate(v):
        e = x if e is None else e + a * (x - e)
        if i >= n - 1:
            out[i] = e
    return out


def _sma(v, n):
    out = [None] * len(v)
    s = 0.0
    for i, x in enumerate(v):
        s += x
        if i >= n:
            s -= v[i - n]
        if i >= n - 1:
            out[i] = s / n
    return out


def _std(v, n):
    out = [None] * len(v)
    s = s2 = 0.0
    for i, x in enumerate(v):
        s += x
        s2 += x * x
        if i >= n:
            y = v[i - n]
            s -= y
            s2 -= y * y
        if i >= n - 1:
            m = s / n
            q = s2 / n - m * m
            out[i] = math.sqrt(q) if q > 0 else 0.0
    return out


def _rext(v, n, want_max):
    out = [None] * len(v)
    dq = deque()
    for i, x in enumerate(v):
        while dq and ((v[dq[-1]] <= x) if want_max else (v[dq[-1]] >= x)):
            dq.pop()
        dq.append(i)
        while dq[0] <= i - n:
            dq.popleft()
        if i >= n - 1:
            out[i] = v[dq[0]]
    return out


def _rules(ctx):
    """The candidate rules whose edges are being estimated. Deliberately
    ordinary and deliberately few: what is under test is the sizing law, not
    the rules, and every extra rule multiplies the bootstrap cost."""
    bars = ctx.bars
    c = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]
    h = [float(b["h"]) for b in bars]
    l = [float(b["l"]) for b in bars]
    n = len(c)
    out = []

    e10, e50 = _ema(c, 10), _ema(c, 50)
    out.append([0 if (e10[i] is None or e50[i] is None) else
                (1 if e10[i] > e50[i] else -1) for i in range(n)])

    uh, ul = _rext(h, 20, True), _rext(l, 20, False)
    br = [0] * n
    st = 0
    for i in range(1, n):
        u, d = uh[i - 1], ul[i - 1]
        if u is not None and c[i] > u:
            st = 1
        elif d is not None and c[i] < d:
            st = -1
        br[i] = st
    out.append(br)

    m50, s50 = _sma(c, 50), _std(c, 50)
    out.append([0 if (m50[i] is None or not s50[i]) else
                (1 if (c[i] - m50[i]) / s50[i] < -1.5 else
                 (-1 if (c[i] - m50[i]) / s50[i] > 1.5 else 0)) for i in range(n)])

    out.append([0 if i < 20 else (1 if c[i] > c[i - 20] else
                                  (-1 if c[i] < c[i - 20] else 0)) for i in range(n)])
    return out


def family_init(ctx):
    """Politis-Romano stationary bootstrap turned into an arming law.

    Each rule's own per-bar P&L is resampled B times with GEOMETRIC block
    lengths of mean 1/q -- geometric rather than fixed is what keeps the
    resampled series stationary, and blocks rather than IID draws are what
    stops the confidence interval collapsing on autocorrelated,
    heteroskedastic trading P&L. The 10th percentile of the resampled Sharpe
    distribution, SR_lcb, is the estimation-risk-aware read on the edge, and
    the rule carries weight w = clip(SR_lcb / SR_point, 0, 1) * f_kelly:
    two rules with the same point Sharpe get different weights when one of
    them got there on a wilder path.

    WHAT SIZING BECOMES HERE. Position size belongs to the shared harness, so
    the risk fraction is expressed as the weight the rule carries in the vote
    and the traded signal is the sign of the w-weighted sum. That preserves
    exactly the part of the law that can be tested from a signal -- a rule
    with a wide Sharpe interval loses influence, and one with SR_lcb <= 0
    loses its vote entirely -- and it makes f_kelly inert, because a constant
    factor cannot change the sign of a sum. f_kelly is kept as a declared
    parameter and deliberately NOT swept for that reason. The annualisation
    constant cancels out of SR_lcb / SR_point and out of the sign of SR_lcb,
    so the Sharpes here are per-bar.

    COST. Block sums come from prefix sums, so a resample costs O(T*q) rather
    than O(T), and one set of block draws is shared across the rules (common
    random numbers, which also makes the weights comparable). The maximum
    drawdown of a resample is therefore measured at BLOCK resolution -- the
    equity path sampled at block boundaries -- which is the one honest
    approximation in here and is stated as such.
    """
    pos = _rules(ctx)
    K = len(pos)
    c = [float(b["c"]) for b in ctx.bars]
    n = len(c)

    T = max(120, int(ctx.p.boot_win))
    B = max(20, int(ctx.p.n_boot))
    blk = max(2, int(ctx.p.blk))
    pct = float(ctx.p.pct) / 100.0
    fk = float(ctx.p.f_kelly)
    recomp = max(50, int(ctx.p.recompute))
    dead_n = int(ctx.p.dead_n)
    use_dd = int(ctx.p.dd_stop)
    ddp = float(ctx.p.dd_pct) / 100.0
    stop_bars = max(1, int(ctx.p.stop_bars))
    lg = math.log(1.0 - 1.0 / blk) if blk > 1 else -1.0

    r = [0.0] * n
    for i in range(1, n):
        if c[i - 1]:
            r[i] = c[i] / c[i - 1] - 1.0

    # per-bar P&L of each rule, and its cumulative path
    pnl = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(K)]
    cum = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(K)]
    for k in range(K):
        pk = pos[k]
        a = pnl[k]
        cu = cum[k]
        s = 0.0
        for i in range(1, n):
            x = pk[i - 1] * r[i]
            a[i] = x
            s += x
            cu[i] = s

    # live drawdown measured over the same T bars the resamples are long
    ddlive = [None] * K
    for k in range(K):
        pk = _rext(cum[k], T, True)
        ddlive[k] = [None if pk[i] is None else (pk[i] - cum[k][i])
                     for i in range(n)]

    seed = int(ctx.p.seed) & 0x7FFFFFFF
    st = seed if seed else 12345

    w = [0.0] * K
    zeros = [0] * K
    dead = [False] * K
    ddcap = [None] * K
    halted = [-1] * K
    sig = [0.0] * n

    for i in range(n):
        if i >= T + 20 and (i - T - 20) % recomp == 0:
            lo = i - T + 1
            S = [0.0] * (T + 1)
            Q = [0.0] * (T + 1)
            # one set of draws, reused across rules
            draws = []
            for _ in range(B):
                bl = []
                got = 0
                while got < T:
                    st = (1103515245 * st + 12345) & 0x7FFFFFFF
                    s0 = st % T
                    st = (1103515245 * st + 12345) & 0x7FFFFFFF
                    u = (st + 1.0) / 2147483649.0
                    L = 1 + int(math.log(u) / lg)
                    if L > T:
                        L = T
                    if got + L > T:
                        L = T - got
                    bl.append((s0, L))
                    got += L
                draws.append(bl)

            for k in range(K):
                if dead[k]:
                    w[k] = 0.0
                    continue
                a = pnl[k]
                s = q = 0.0
                for j in range(T):
                    x = a[lo + j]
                    s += x
                    q += x * x
                    S[j + 1] = s
                    Q[j + 1] = q
                m = s / T
                var = q / T - m * m
                if var <= 0.0:
                    w[k] = 0.0
                    continue
                sd = math.sqrt(var * T / (T - 1.0))
                sr_pt = m / sd
                srs = []
                dds = []
                for bl in draws:
                    tot = tq = 0.0
                    cu = 0.0
                    peak = 0.0
                    dd = 0.0
                    for (s0, L) in bl:
                        e = s0 + L
                        if e <= T:
                            bs = S[e] - S[s0]
                            bq = Q[e] - Q[s0]
                        else:
                            e -= T
                            bs = (S[T] - S[s0]) + S[e]
                            bq = (Q[T] - Q[s0]) + Q[e]
                        tot += bs
                        tq += bq
                        cu += bs
                        if cu > peak:
                            peak = cu
                        elif peak - cu > dd:
                            dd = peak - cu
                    mm = tot / T
                    vv = tq / T - mm * mm
                    if vv <= 0.0:
                        continue
                    srs.append(mm / math.sqrt(vv * T / (T - 1.0)))
                    dds.append(dd)
                if len(srs) < 10:
                    w[k] = 0.0
                    continue
                srs.sort()
                dds.sort()
                lcb = srs[min(len(srs) - 1, int(pct * (len(srs) - 1)))]
                ddcap[k] = dds[min(len(dds) - 1, int(ddp * (len(dds) - 1)))]
                if lcb <= 0.0 or sr_pt <= 0.0:
                    w[k] = 0.0
                    zeros[k] += 1
                    if dead_n and zeros[k] >= dead_n:
                        dead[k] = True
                else:
                    x = lcb / sr_pt
                    w[k] = (0.0 if x <= 0.0 else (1.0 if x > 1.0 else x)) * fk
                    zeros[k] = 0

        tot = 0.0
        for k in range(K):
            if not w[k] or dead[k]:
                continue
            if use_dd:
                if halted[k] > i:
                    continue
                cap = ddcap[k]
                dl = ddlive[k][i]
                if cap is not None and dl is not None and dl > cap:
                    halted[k] = i + stop_bars   # deeper than the rule's own history
                    continue
            tot += w[k] * pos[k][i]
        sig[i] = 1.0 if tot > 0 else (-1.0 if tot < 0 else 0.0)

    ctx.sig = ctx.series(sig, "lcb_vote")


def signal(ctx, i):
    s = ctx.sig[i]
    return 1 if s > 0 else (-1 if s < 0 else 0)
